definition: For each funding settlement T of a perpetual paying F_T: dprem = prem(T+5m) - prem(T-5m), prem = perp/index - 1; pass-through beta = E[sign(F) dprem] / E[|F|]. Rule: when the previous rate |F_hat| >= theta and the 5-minute quote volume before entry >= 100,000, take s = -sign(F_hat) from T-5m to T+5m; net = s r_perp - s F_T - 2c.
disappears_when: In the dead zone of Binance's formula (F = 0.01%), as timing bots compete for it, if the exchange prorates funding to the time held, or once an index hedge is cheap enough for arbitrageurs to enforce the jump.
holding_and_risk: Ten minutes across each settlement. Unhedged exposure to the contract's price for those minutes, and to a settled rate of another sign or size than the previous one, which chose the side.
mechanism: A perpetual is a zero-cost contract that pays a lump cash flow F_T at known times. Without frictions its price must move by the payment across T, as a share goes ex-dividend, so its premium over the index jumps by F_T. Only traders who time their positions around T enforce that jump; those who hold through settlements do not trade at T.
name: EXF-1 ex-funding pass-through
participants: Created by leveraged holders who pay or receive funding through every settlement without timing it (most of the open interest); left in place by the costs and risk of the timing traders and arbitrageurs who would remove it.
predictions: the premium moves across T by beta F_T with beta measurably below 1 where |F_T| >= 0.1%
the receiving side's net is positive after 10 bp fills at some threshold of |F_hat|
the same trade at a quarter, a half and three quarters of the interval earns nothing comparable
refuted_if: beta is indistinguishable from 1 where |F| is large
the placebo windows earn as much as the settlement window
the net does not survive fills of 20 bp
return_relation: E[net | F_hat] = sign(F_hat) E[(1 - beta) F_T] - E[sign(F_hat) r_index] - 2c: positive only where (1 - beta)|F_T| exceeds two fills.

vs_failed.funding carry: the carry programs held the receiving side for days and lost to the premium's drift and the round trip; this holds ten minutes, its edge is the unpriced fraction of one payment, and it must beat placebo windows where no payment falls

why_exists: Enforcing the jump needs traders who close before T and reopen after, paying two fills, or arbitrageurs who hold the paying side across T and carry ten minutes of the contract's risk. Where they are few relative to the payment, the price passes on less than the payment.
why_not_competed_away: It is capacity-limited (minutes around T, only where |F| is large: crowded and often thin contracts), needs unhedged price risk in volatile contracts, and pays taker fees twice: large funds cannot scale it and small ones pay wide spreads.
